Snippets are executed by scripts/guides.cjs: the pure-Python shape/aggregation examples run and their real stdout is stored, while the numpy/pandas snippets are marked verified:false (linux-style 'bundled runtime' note in the UI) because those modules are not installed on this machine.

guides.title: NumPy Arrays, Shape & Broadcasting
guides.what: NumPy array ek fixed-dtype, contiguous n-dimensional buffer hai. Shape (dimensions ka tuple), dtype aur axis — ye teen cheezein samajh lo to baaki sab numpy predictable lagne lagta hai.
guides.why: Array operations C speed me chalti hain aur vectorized code loop se dash guna tez hota hai. Shape aur dtype ka concept ML code me har jagah chahiye — galat shape hi silent bug ka sabse bada source hai.
guides.whereUsed: Feature matrices, embeddings, image tensors, normalization aur batching — numpy se sklearn/torch tak ka data flow.
guides.howItWorks: Array ki shape right se left align hoti hai; har dimension ya equal honi chahiye ya 1 (broadcasting). Aggregation (sum/mean) axis par hoti hai: axis=0 rows ko mila deta hai (column-wise result) aur axis=1 across-row chalta hai — result ki shape ek dimension kam ho jati hai.
guides.syntax:
import numpy as np
a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])      # shape (2, 2)
a.shape, a.dtype, a.ndim
a.mean(axis=0)                       # per-column
a.reshape(4)
a * 2                                # elementwise, no loop
b = a.astype(np.float32)             # downcast = half memory

explain: Rules ko ek chhote pure-Python function me likha gaya hai, isliye broadcasting ka logic aankhon se verify ho jata hai.
zip shorter tuple par ruk jata hai — missing dimension ko 1 maan lena hi asli broadcasting rule hai.
(3, 2) + (4,) fail karta hai kyunki 2 aur 4 na barabar hain na 1 — yahi classic shape error hai.
(3, 1, 4) + (4,) chalta hai: 1 kisi bhi size se align ho jata hai.

examples.code:
import numpy as np

a = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
print(a.shape, a.dtype, a.ndim)
print(a.mean(axis=0), a.mean(axis=1))
print(a.reshape(4), a.sum())
print((a * 2 + 1).tolist())
explain: shape (2, 2) batata hai 2 rows aur 2 columns hain; dtype int64 hai kyunki input integers the.
axis=0 columns ka mean deta hai ([2, 3]) aur axis=1 rows ka ([1.5, 3.5]) — dono ka result shape (2,) hai.
reshape(4) flat view deta hai; sum() scalar total (10) lauta deta hai.
a * 2 + 1 elementwise chalta hai — vectorized expression, koi explicit loop nahi.

examples.code:
import numpy as np

rows = np.arange(1_000_000, dtype=np.float64)
squared = rows ** 2
print(squared.dtype, squared.nbytes)
small = squared.astype(np.float32)
print(small.dtype, small.nbytes)
print("approx mean:", float(small.mean()))
print("vectorized, no python loop:", squared[:3].tolist())
examples.output:
float64 8000000
float32 4000000
approx mean: 3.3333332e+11
vectorized, no python loop: [0.0, 1.0, 4.0]
explain: nbytes = elements x itemsize: 10 lakh float64 = 8 MB, float32 = 4 MB — dtype downcast se memory aadhi.
Vectorized expression ek hi C loop me chalta hai; Python loop se 10-100x tez aur memory-safe rehta hai.
float32 par bade numbers ki precision ghate hai — isliye mean ko '_approx_' bolna honest hai.

howToCode.detail: Kaam shuru karne se pehle expected shape aur dtype likho (comment ya assert me). Aadhe numpy bugs isi ek line se pakde jaate hain.
Elementwise loop ko array expression me badlo; aggregation ke liye sum/mean + axis use karo.

howToCode.step: axis ko naam se test karo
howToCode.detail: Chhote 2x3 array par axis=0 aur axis=1 ka output print karo — yaad rakhne se better hai ek baar dekh lena.
Slicing view deti hai, fancy indexing copy deti hai; agar memory tight hai to views aur out= parameters use karo.

commonMistakes: shape mismatch ko ignore karna — broadcasting silently galat result deti hai jab dim 1 ho.
axis=0 aur axis=1 ko ulta samajhna (row vs column collapse).
Chhote numeric types ko poori range ke liye use karna (int8 me overflow warn nahi karta).
Dtype object (strings) par arithmetic karna — slow aur galat.
Normalization me constant column (std = 0) par division — NaN/inf propagate.
bestPractices: Har transform ke baad light asserts: shape, dtype, NaN count, range.
Dtype explicitly choose karo (np.float32) — memory aur speed dono.
Bade arrays me in-place operations ya out= parameter use karo.
Random operations me seed pin karo — reproducible results eval ke liye zaroori hai.
guides.realWorld: Ek 10 lakh row feature matrix ka normalization, image batch ka resize/augment, aur embedding ka cosine similarity — teeno vectorized numpy/BLAS se chalte hain, Python loop se nahi. Interview me 'maine dtype float32 kiya aur memory aadhi ho gayi' ka concrete number strong signal hai.

practice.text: Ek 2x3 array banao aur axis=0 / axis=1 ka sum print karo; dono result ki shape likho.
Column-wise z-score normalization implement karo aur constant column (std=0) ko safely handle karo.
Ek batching function likho jo (N, D) array ko (N/B, B, D) chunks me tode aur bacha hua last chunk bhi handle kare.

interview.a: Right se left align karte hain; har dimension equal ho ya 1 ho. Missing dimension ko 1 maana jata hai. Isse (3,2)+(3,1) chalta hai par (3,2)+(4,) fail hota hai.
axis=0 par rows collapse hoti hain (per-column result), axis=1 par columns collapse hote hain (per-row result) — result ki shape dono case me ek dimension chhoti ho jati hai.

interview.q: Copy aur view ka farq performance ke liye?
interview.a: Basic slicing view deti hai (koi copy nahi, sasta), fancy/boolean indexing copy banati hai — bade arrays me ye memory aur speed ka farq ban jata hai.

guides.miniChallenge: NumPy ke bina, pure Python me ek mini broadcasting engine likho jo do nested lists ko rule ke hisaab se add kar sake ya clear error de.
guides.debugTask: Normalization ke baad array me NaN aa gaye (mean 0, std 0 wala column). Reproduce karo, root cause batao aur guard likho.
revision: shape = dimensions ka tuple; nbytes = elements x itemsize
float32 = half memory, thodi precision kam
guides.interviewTip: Shape-related sawal par ye bolo: 'main pehle expected shape likhta hoon aur har transform ke baad assert karta hoon — kyunki numpy shape errors silent hote hain'.

guides.title: Pandas DataFrame Workflow
guides.what: DataFrame ek labeled 2D table hai (Series = ek column). Real workflow: load → inspect (shape/dtypes/nulls) → clean/transform → groupby/merge → aggregate → report.
guides.why: Data analysis ka 80% kaam tabular cleaning aur aggregation hai. dtype/null/grain ki galti poori report galat kar deti hai, isliye inspection-first workflow aana chahiye.
guides.whereUsed: CSV/Excel/sql ingestion, feature tables, KPI reports, train/test split ke pehle ka cleaning step.
guides.howItWorks: DataFrame andar column-wise numpy arrays rakhta hai, isliye column select karke vectorized operations sasti hoti hain. groupby ek split-apply-combine karta hai aur result us key par indexed hota hai; join/merge normalized keys par rows ko match karta hai aur duplicate keys par rows fan-out ho jaati hain.
guides.syntax:
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv(path, usecols=[...], dtype={...})
df.shape, df.dtypes, df.isna().sum()
df[df["amount"] > 0]
df.groupby("region")["amount"].sum().reset_index(name="revenue")
left.merge(right, on="id", how="left", validate="one_to_many")

examples.code:
# groupby ka core idea, bina pandas ke — ek pass me per-key total
rows = [("east", 10.0), ("west", 5.0), ("east", 7.0)]

totals = {}
for region, amount in rows:
    totals[region] = totals.get(region, 0) + amount

print(totals)
print(sorted(totals.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1]))
print(sum(totals.values()))
explain: groupby ka essence yahi hai: ek key par split karo aur values apply karke combine karo — pandas isi ko C speed me karta hai.
Sorted output se 'best region' turant dikh jata hai (descending order).
Total ko reconcile karna (sum of groups = overall total) report ki honesty check hai.

examples.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("orders.csv", usecols=["region", "amount"], dtype={"amount": "float32"})
print(df.shape, df.dtypes.to_dict())
print(df.isna().sum().to_dict())
clean = df.dropna(subset=["amount"]).copy()
clean["amount"] = clean["amount"].clip(lower=0)
g = clean.groupby("region")["amount"].sum().reset_index(name="revenue")
print(g.sort_values("revenue", ascending=False).head().to_dict("records"))
print(round(g["revenue"].sum(), 2), round(clean["amount"].sum(), 2))
explain: usecols se sirf zaroori columns padhte hain aur dtype se memory kam — bade CSV me ye pehla optimization hai.
isna().sum() ke baad NaN rows drop karna: numerator/denominator ka basis alag na ho jaye.
groupby ke baad reset_index() flat table banata hai, isliye plot/export karna aasan ho jata hai.
Do totals barabar hone se confirm hota hai ki grouping ne kuch giraa nahi (reconciliation).

examples.code:
import pandas as pd

left = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "region": ["e", "w", "e"]})
right = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 1, 2], "amount": [5.0, 7.0, 3.0]})

print(right["id"].duplicated().tolist())
print(len(left), "left rows")

agg = right.groupby("id")["amount"].sum().reset_index()
merged = left.merge(agg, on="id", how="left", validate="one_to_one")
merged["amount"] = merged["amount"].fillna(0.0)
print(len(left), len(merged), round(merged["amount"].sum(), 2))
print(right["amount"].sum())
explain: duplicated() right table me key 1 do baar hone ki warning deta hai — yehi merge fan-out ka source hai.
Merge se pehle right side ko groupby se unique kar liya, isliye rows multiply nahi hui.
validate='one_to_one' galat cardinality par exception raise karta hai — row count chup-chaap badhne nahi deta.
Donon totals (merged vs original) barabar hone se confirm hota hai ki sum double-count nahi hua.

howToCode.detail: Load karte hi shape, dtypes aur null counts print karo — 'numbers dikh rahe hain' ka matlab dtype numeric hai, aisa maan lena bug hai.
'1 row = kya?' ye likho (ek order? ek order-item?). Grain galat ho to har aggregate galat hoga.

howToCode.step: Merge se pehle keys clean karo
howToCode.detail: Join key par duplicates check karo, warna fan-out hoga aur totals inflate ho jayenge.
Grouped total aur overall total compare karo — mismatch ka matlab drop ya double count hua hai.

commonMistakes: dtype galat chhod dena (numbers object ban jate hain, phir sum concatenate karta hai).
Merge ke baad row count na check karna (fan-out se totals double).
Chained assignment (df[df.a > 0]['b'] = 1) — SettingWithCopyWarning aur silent no-op.
NaN ko mean ke saath mix karna: skipna se numerator/denominator ka basis alag ho jata hai.
join/merge ke bina grain document kiye top-N report karna (ties aadha adhoora count dete hain).
bestPractices: Load karte waqt usecols + dtype do — memory aur speed dono.
Transform ke baad assertions lagao: shape, null counts, key uniqueness.
Aggregate karte waqt reset_index() se flat output banao.
Merges me validate= set karo (one_to_one/one_to_many) taaki cardinality bug turant dikhe.
Bade data ke liye chunks ya agg-first approach use karo.
guides.realWorld: KPI dashboard jo CSV se per-region revenue banata hai, ML feature table jo orders aur customers join karti hai, aur p95 latency ki report — sab isi workflow se bante hain. Interview me 'main merge se pehle key duplicates check karta hoon' bolna correctness-first mindset dikhata hai.

practice.text: Ek DataFrame par shape, dtypes aur null counts print karo aur batao kaun sa column aage todega.
orders aur customers ko merge karo, fan-out se bacho aur per-customer revenue nikalo.
10 lakh row CSV ko chunks me padhkar per-region total nikalo aur poora data memory me load na karo.

interview.q: Merge ke baad row count badh gaya — kya check karoge?
interview.a: Join key me duplicates (fan-out). df[key].duplicated().any() se confirm karo, duplicated side ko pehle groupby se unique karo, aur merge me validate= lagao.

interview.q: groupby ka result kaisa hota hai?
interview.a: Series/DataFrame jiska index group key hota hai. Flat table ke liye reset_index() lagao — warna aage merge/plot me shape confusion hoti hai.
mean/median NaN skip karte hain par count me unhe ginnta hi nahi, isliye numerator aur denominator ka basis alag ho jata hai — null counts ke saath hi aggregate report karo.

guides.miniChallenge: Ek clean_orders(df) function likho jo dtype fix kare, negative amounts ko clip kare, key duplicates par warn kare aur ek report dict return kare.
guides.debugTask: Dashboard ka total sahih hai par per-region totals ka sum mismatch hai. Sabse pehle kya check karoge, aur fix kya hoga?
revision: Merge se pehle key uniqueness check
guides.interviewTip: Interview me data question ka jawab inspection se shuru karo: 'shape, dtypes aur nulls dekhne ke baad main grain fix karta hoon' — ye structured approach instantly alag dikhta hai.
